notes: Summary: NorthBloom is evaluating Dedicated + Private deployment for latency-sensitive retail personalization and chat. Goal: predictable unit economics + airtight SLA for peak shopping seasons.
Business drivers: reduce checkout friction, real-time product reranking, 24/7 support chat across US/EU.
Capacity ask: baseline reserved pool = 8x A100 equivalent GPUs (commit), ability to burst +20% during Black Friday windows; planning guidance requested from Redwood on burst credit consumption.
Throughput & latency targets: target steady-state throughput 10k tokens/sec across reserved pool; p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms for 512-token conversational payloads (chat model).
- Uptime target proposal: 99.95% for dedicated capacity; NorthBloom pushing for 99.97% during peak season windows.

- Credit schedule: tiered credits based on monthly uptime (example proposed by legal): 99.95-99.99 = 10% service credit, 99.9-99.95 = 25%, <99.9 = 50% (NorthBloom requests faster escalations for sub-99.9).

- Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance <= 2 hours/month, with 30 days notice; emergency maintenance only with compensating credits if outside agreed calendar-tagged maintenance blackout periods.
- Support SLAs: P1 response 15 minutes (phone + Slack), P2 response 1 hour, P3 next-business-day; 24/7 escalation for production incidents during peak campaign windows.

- Performance SLOs: per-model p95 latency guarantees and throughput floors per reserved GPU; auto-fallback to smaller model variant allowed but must be flagged and credited if quality/regression happens.
Security & compliance: require SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML integration, customer-managed KMS, audit log retention 12 months, and option for EU data residency for EU customers (legal redline).

POC results: two-week POC on 4x A100s in Redwood Dedicated - observed p95 ~ 165ms for chat 512 tokens; sustained throughput ~4.8k tokens/sec. NorthBloom wants linear scaling guidance for +4 GPUs and predictable p95 under concurrent sessions.
Notes from call (2026-03-02): 'We need guarantees for Black Friday — if you cannot commit to credits and timed maintenance blackout, our procurement cannot sign.' — Head of Infrastructure.

Open items for legal redline: warranty language around planned vs unplanned downtime, definition of "Available" (API level vs model-level vs infra-level), force majeure carveouts, and SLA measurement windows (UTC vs customer local).

Operational asks: runbook handover, canary schedule for minor releases (24-hour canary with 5% traffic), rollback guarantees, and a pre-approved test harness for performance regressions tied to credits.

Next commercial asks: tailored pricing for reserved commitment (12-month term) with built-in burst pool credits, and an optional add-on for extended observability (30-day token-level retention) to be included in negotiation.

Short-term next steps: legal to exchange redlines by 2026-03-15; AE/SE to deliver a confirmed GPU planning appendix with cost and scaling curves by 2026-03-12; schedule procurement review week of 2026-03-22.
